# Ranking reversal between TSB-NB and LGB-Q on VN1, by warehouse (generated by code/ranking_reversal.py)

Outcome y = log(inventory TSB-NB / inventory LGB-Q) at fill 0.92 within a warehouse (≥ 20 series); y < 0: TSB-NB needs less stock. Predictors: pre-test medians only.

## 1. Outcome and univariate associations (Spearman ρ of y with each predictor)

| window | warehouses with y | share y < 0 | median y | recent_ratio_13 | trend_26 | log_adi | cv2 | zero_share | hist_len | log_mean | log_n |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| third | 53 | 70% | -0.135 | -0.04 | -0.06 | +0.34 | +0.30 | +0.34 | -0.40 | -0.25 | +0.23 |
| second | 85 | 54% | -0.026 | -0.27 | +0.19 | +0.04 | +0.32 | +0.04 | -0.02 | +0.01 | +0.07 |
| main | 90 | 56% | -0.022 | -0.10 | -0.17 | +0.05 | +0.09 | +0.05 | -0.15 | -0.07 | -0.15 |

## 2–3. Out-of-window prediction and decision value

| fit on → test on | Spearman ρ (pred, y) | permutation p | warehouses assigned TSB-NB | inventory vs always LGB-Q | oracle by warehouse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| third → second | +0.27 | 0.015 | 77 of 109 | -9.4% | -10.6% |
| second → main | +0.22 | 0.037 | 78 of 145 | -0.2% | -7.1% |
| third + second → main | +0.21 | 0.046 | 86 of 145 | +2.9% | -7.1% |

Negative inventory change = the rule needs less stock than LGB-Q everywhere at portfolio fill 0.92. The oracle uses each warehouse's realised y in the test window and is not deployable.
